M/S L And A Cafe vs The State Of Telangana on 22 September,
2025
 The Honourable Sri Justice N.V.Shravan Kumar
 Writ Petition Nos.3678 and 24222 of 2025
Common Order:

entities.text: M/S L And A Cafe vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and Sri M.Srinivas, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home appearing for respondents.
With their consent these writ petitions are taken up for disposal at the admission stage itself.

2. W.P.No.3678 of 2025 is filed seeking following prayer:-
"to issue a proper writ, order or orders particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the respondents No.1 to 7 in interfering with the petitioners business F3 CAFE situated at H.No.1-62/K/1/44, 4th and 5th Floor,
Kavuri Hills, Guttala Begumpet, Jubliee Hills, Hyderabad as illegal, arbitrary highhanded apart from being violative of Articles 14 and 19 1 g of Constitution of India consequently direct the respondents not to interfere with the petitioner business F3 CAFE situated at H.No.1-62/K/1/44, 4th and 5th Floor, Kavuri Hills,
Guttala Begumpet, Jubliee Hills, Hyderabad."
3. W.P.No.24222 of 2025 is filed seeking following prayer:-
"to issue a writ order or direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus direct the respondents herein to allow the petitioner to earmark his designated smoking area as per the COTPA Act and to allow his clientele to use the same as they please as long as they are following the same COTPA Act, 2003 in the name and style as M/s. L and A Cafe Situated at Door No.2-65/SVA/100, SV Arcade,
Sy.No.54/A and 54/E, Khajaguda Main Road, Circle No.20, Serilingampally,
Hyderabad, without reference to rule law or regulations as illegal arbitrary unconstitutional and contrary to the provisions of COTP Act and consequently direct the respondents to permit the petitioner to continue his business of serving flavoured Hookahs in his shop in the name and style as M/s. L and A Cafe Situated at Door No.2-65/SVA/100, SV Arcade, Sy.No.54/A and 54/E, Khajaguda Main Road, Circle No.20, Serilingampally, Hyderabad without any hindrance or restrictions."

4. Brief facts stated in these writ petitions are that petitioners are running a caf in the subject premises and are having license to carry out the business of caf/restaurant and as a part of business, petitioners also offers food and beverages, and also intends to offer flavoured hookah services to the customers as per norms and conditions.

Petitioners are also having trade licenses from the GHMC and also license from the Government of Telangana Food Safety and Standards M/S L And A Cafe vs The State Of Telangana on 22 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88678180/
1 Authority of India.

sentences.text: It is submitted that respondent authorities had interfered with the business of the petitioners and not allowing to run the business.
Questioning the same these writ petitions are filed.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that this Court vide common order dated 15.11.2023 in W.P.No.8223 of 2013 and batch, passed the following order:-
"24.
In view of the above discussion, this Court is of the opinion that imposing of certain conditions to run the Hookah Centres would meet the ends of justice.

i) As Charcoal is being used for serving hookah in the Hookah Centres, the petitioners shall obtain licence from the Municipal Corporation as specified under Section 521(1)(b) of Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation Act, 1955.

ii) Since the Hyderabad City Police Act, 1348 Fasli confers power over the amusement Centres/restaurants which are defined as "public place" under the COTP Act and as per Rule 4 of the Prohibition of Smoking in Public Places Rules, 2008 permission is required specifying smoking area.

entities.text: Prohibition of Smoking in Public Places Rules, 2008
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: Therefore, to establish hookah centres, the petitioners shall obtain necessary permission from the concerned authority under the provisions of the City Police Act.
iii) The Hookah Centres are prohibited from serving any tobacco product to the persons below the age of eighteen years.
Pictorial health-warning labels at the entrance must be displayed.

iv) The respondents-police are at liberty to supervise and inspect the Hookah Centres, for any violation of rules and regulations, guidelines or circulars issued under the provisions of the Hyderabad City Police Act, 1348 Fasli.
v) If there is any violation of the provisions of the COTP Act and the Rules made thereunder, the respondents-police are at liberty to take appropriate action as per the provisions of the COTP Act.

25. Subject to fulfilling the above conditions and also the provisions of COTP Act, the respondents-police are directed not to interfere with the business activity of the petitioners for running Hookah Centres.

If the police are found to act in a highhanded manner, the owners of the Hookah Centres are at liberty to bring the same to the notice of the Director General of Police/Commissioner of Police, as directed by this Court in Writ Petition No.3202 of 2014 and batch, in which event the said authority shall forthwith take necessary steps in that regard.
26. Accordingly, all these Writ Petitions are disposed of."

5. The case of the petitioners is that though they have obtained all necessary permissions from various authorities to run the business and in spite of the common order dated 15.11.2023 passed in W.P.No.8223 of 2013 and batch, the respondent authorities are interfering in their business.

2 6.

entities.text: L And A Cafe vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Recording the submission made by the learned counsel appearing on either side and in terms of Common order dated 15.11.2023 in W.P.No.8223 of 2013 and batch, these writ petitions are disposed of leaving it open to the respondent authorities to pass appropriate orders, if any representation are made by the petitioners.
7. Miscellaneous applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
No order as to costs.

JUSTICE N.V.SHRAVAN KUMAR Date:
